children.text: Every design and implementation decision is subordinate to these two, which a reviewer will
1. **Run once → `kill -9` during the QC stage → restart.** It must resume from the checkpoint,
2. **Run again.** It must detect that there is **no new data** and not re-ingest.
- The stage machine is persisted **outside the process** (SQLite). Each episode's stage advance
is **its own transaction** — never "write everything at the end of the run".
- Every write is idempotent. Idempotency key: `(source_id, upstream_id, content_hash)`.
- Artifacts are written `*.tmp` → fsync file → fsync dir → `os.replace()`. **File first, DB
state second.** A crash in between must leave a state the re-run can idempotently redo.
If a change makes either scenario harder to satisfy, the change is wrong regardless of how clean
- `docs/technical_design.md` is the spec. **Read the relevant section before implementing.**
- **While a component has no code, the design wins.** Once code exists, the code is the truth for
_what is_ and the design is the truth for _what should be_.
So: **unify the structure, never the numbers.** Any instinct to squash everything into one
fixed-width vector is wrong and is explicitly rejected by the design.
**This repository currently contains documentation only. There is no code yet.**
docs/technical_design.md      # the design authority — domain model, schema, QC, layering
docs/implementation_plan.md   # milestones M0–M8, each with verification commands
docs/ai_chat_sessions/*.json  # raw AI transcripts — archival, do not edit or translate
Everything under `src/`, `tests/`, `config/`, and `scripts/` described below **does not exist
yet**. Create it milestone by milestone per the implementation plan; do not scaffold the whole

children.text: # Source registry. Committed — no absolute local paths, no credentials.
# `max_episodes` caps are data-driven, from the M0 spike measurements recorded in
# docs/adr/000-source-selection.md. frames/episode below are measured, not guessed.
with_video: false # see design §1: video metadata only by default
# A — 2D planar pushing, absolute task-space xy in PIXELS. Not an arm.
LeRobot codebase_version v3.0: all episodes share one parquet file and one mp4;
episode boundaries come from meta/episodes. Channel names motor_0/motor_1 are
misleading and are overridden by config/embodiments.yaml.
# B — ALOHA bimanual, absolute joint angles (rad) + 2 grippers. Same format as A.
max_episodes: 50 # measured exactly 500 frames/episode @50 Hz -> 25.0k frames
Every episode is exactly 500 frames (10 s), so termination is a step limit,
and there is no success or reward column at all.
# C — OXE / RLDS. End-effector delta pose + gripper command + terminate flag.
reader: tfrecord_direct # see docs/adr/001-rlds-reader.md: no TensorFlow
# 512-D per-step derivative, recomputable from the text; see design §A.C.6
No stable upstream episode id: identity is (split, shard, index-in-shard), so
content_hash must be computed over normalized episode bytes, not shard bytes.
# D — EPIC-KITCHENS-100, taken by layer. Action is an episode-level symbolic label.
license: cc-by-nc-4.0 # non-commercial; propagates to export lines
max_episodes: 60 # action segments, ~3 s each -> ~9k frames @50 fps
# Frame indices are derived from seconds at the EXTRACTION fps, which is NOT the video's
# official fps: 50 fps videos were extracted at 50, everything else at a flat 60.
# Measured against all 67,217 train segments (100% reproduced). See ADR 004.
videos: # spread across participants; deliberately mixes IMU present/absent
- P01_01 # EPIC-55 era, official 59.94 fps: no GoPro metadata -> has_imu=false
- P01_101 # extension, official 50 fps: has GoPro metadata -> has_imu=true
- P28_101 # EPIC-Fields example reconstruction is published for this video
Seconds are authoritative, frame indices are derived. The local 30 fps transcode is a
mirror, registered in config/sources.local.yaml, never an authoritative source.

magnitude of a mostly-stationary accelerometer.

under spikes/_data/ is gitignored.

cd /Users/wanghuan/Documents/py_repos/luma_ai_assessment && git add docs/adr config/sources.yaml docs/technical_design.md docs/implementation_plan.md AGENTS.md && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
docs(adr): record M0 findings and resync the design with measured data

M0 is complete: four sources confirmed reachable with no substitution, and the
two facts the design flagged as unverified are now answered by measurement.

The spike contradicted the design in four places, so each correction lands as an
ADR plus the matching design edit in the same change (DoD gate 7):

  000  final source selection; max_episodes caps derived from measured episode
       lengths (~50k frames, superseding the 80k-120k target: B has only 50
       episodes upstream, so a bigger corpus would just be more of source A)
  001  TFDS is unusable, so C is read by parsing TFRecord directly - no
       TensorFlow in production, and byte-range reads become possible
  002  LeRobot is v3.0 (many episodes per parquet, one mp4 per dataset,
       boundaries in meta/episodes), and terminated vs truncated does not
       survive the export for A or B -> is_truncated is None, now in section 11
  003  C's action is 8-D, not 10-D (terminate_episode is a scalar), and its
       gripper is a ternary change command, not an absolute position. So
       is_delta differs between B's and C's gripper channels within the same
       role, which strengthens the case for channel-level semantics
  004  EPIC's frame indices use an extraction fps that is not the video's
       official fps (50 fps videos at 50, everything else at a flat 60:
       100.00% of 67,217 segments reproduced, against 58.1% for official fps).
       IMU units measured: accel m/s^2 (mean |a| = 9.8998), gyro rad/s, 195 Hz

Appendix A now quotes what the probes actually read instead of documentation.
config/sources.yaml pins P01_01 and P01_101 so that "capabilities differ per
episode within one source" stays reproducible rather than incidental.
MSG

spike(m0): probe all four sources against real data

Throwaway probes, kept in git so every number in the M0 ADRs is reproducible:

  uv run --group spike python spikes/probe_lerobot.py   # sources A and B
  uv run --group spike python spikes/probe_rlds.py      # source C
  uv run --group spike python spikes/probe_epic.py      # source D

probe_rlds parses TFRecord and tf.train.Example by hand because TFDS does not
import (protobuf gencode 6.31 vs runtime 5.29); it asserts that failure rather
than assuming it, by actually calling FeatureConnector.from_json.

probe_epic measures rather than quotes: it tests candidate frame-extraction
rates against all 67,217 train segments, and derives the IMU units from the
magnitude of a mostly-stationary accelerometer.

Captured output is committed under spikes/_out/; the 232 MB of downloaded data
under spikes/_data/ is gitignored.

docs(adr): record M0 findings and resync the design with measured data

M0 is complete: four sources confirmed reachable with no substitution, and the
two facts the design flagged as unverified are now answered by measurement.

The spike contradicted the design in four places, so each correction lands as an
ADR plus the matching design edit in the same change (DoD gate 7):

  000  final source selection; max_episodes caps derived from measured episode
       lengths (~50k frames, superseding the 80k-120k target: B has only 50
       episodes upstream, so a bigger corpus would just be more of source A)
  001  TFDS is unusable, so C is read by parsing TFRecord directly - no
       TensorFlow in production, and byte-range reads become possible
  002  LeRobot is v3.0 (many episodes per parquet, one mp4 per dataset,
       boundaries in meta/episodes), and terminated vs truncated does not
       survive the export for A or B -> is_truncated is None, now in section 11
  003  C's action is 8-D, not 10-D (terminate_episode is a scalar), and its
       gripper is a ternary change command, not an absolute position. So
       is_delta differs between B's and C's gripper channels within the same
       role, which strengthens the case for channel-level semantics
  004  EPIC's frame indices use an extraction fps that is not the video's
       official fps (50 fps videos at 50, everything else at a flat 60:
       100.00% of 67,217 segments reproduced, against 58.1% for official fps).
       IMU units measured: accel m/s^2 (mean |a| = 9.8998), gyro rad/s, 195 Hz

Appendix A now quotes what the probes actually read instead of documentation.
config/sources.yaml pins P01_01 and P01_101 so that "capabilities differ per
episode within one source" stays reproducible rather than incidental.
MSG
